metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-adhd-psyctr: Version 26.0.0
metadata.description:
The data-adhd-psyctr dataset 📊

The data-adhd-psyctr dataset is a meta-analytic research domain (MARD; see the MARD framework paper), part of the Metapsy project. It contains study information and effect size data from randomized trials on behavioral parent or teacher training for children and adolescents with ADHD under the age of 18 years (Hornstra et al., 2022).

The dataset includes studies that compared parent or teacher training with a control condition, as well as studies that compared a multimodal intervention (i.e., a combination of parent, teacher, and/or child training) with a control condition. Reported outcomes (outcome_category) are total ADHD symptoms, separate symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity, and behavioral problems (symptoms of oppositional defiant disorder or conduct disorder).

The following rules were applied during data extraction:

  • When no total ADHD symptom score was available, the separate inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity scores were pooled, and this aggregate was used as a measure of total ADHD symptoms.
  • When a study had multiple measurement points, the outcomes closest to the end date of the intervention were selected.
  • When there were multiple informants, parent-rated outcomes were selected for parent training and teacher-rated outcomes for teacher training. For multimodal interventions, the rating of the informant with whom most training time was spent was selected.
  • When parent-rated outcomes were reported by both parents, the mother-reported outcomes were selected to increase comparability across studies.
  • When the same construct was measured multiple times, the measurement most commonly used across the included studies was selected.

All data were extracted by two independent reviewers. Risk of bias assessments were performed by two independent reviewers using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (version 2).

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.

inclusion: Children and adolescents with ADHD under the age of 18 years meeting clinical cut-offs on ADHD questionnaires or meeting DSM-III (American Psychiatric Association, 1980), DSM-IV (American Psychiatric Association, 1994), DSM-IV-TR (American Psychiatric Association, 2000), or DSM-5 (American Psychiatric Association, 2013) criteria for ADHD on a (semi)structured interview
exclusion: Studies primarily aimed at samples with comorbid ADHD

inclusion: Behavioral parent or teacher training, multimodal intervention (i.e., a combination of parent, teacher, and/or child training)

Control condition was either (i) an active control treatment (i.e., a treatment arm that controls for nonspecific effects of the intervention); (ii) a treatment as usual; (iii) a no treatment/waitlist control. If trials had two control conditions, the condition with the highest quality (defined above i > ii > iii) was selected as the comparison.
exclusion: Medication or intervention arms in which medication was (part of) the treatment

inclusion: Total ADHD symptoms, separate symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity, and behavioral problems (symptoms of oppositional defiant disorder [ODD], or conduct disorder [CD])
Randomized controlled trials (RCTs)

metadata/variable_description.json.study: Author of the study. Formated as: Last name of first author, year
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm1: Type of treatment (HNC= Helping the Noncompliant Child, NFPP= New Forest Parenting Package, Triple-P= Positive Parenting Program, BPT= behavioural parent training, STEPP= Strategies to Enhance Positive Parenting , DRC= daily report card, Coaches= Coaching Our Acting-out Children: Heightening Essential Skills, PSY= psychoeducation, EGTP= Enhanced Group Triple-P, PCIT= Parent-Child Interaction Therapy, FSS(-EE)= Family-School Success(-Early Education), CLS= Collaborative Life Skills, CLAS= Child Life and Attention Skills, PFT= parent-focused treatment, WPJ= Well Parent Japan, STAND= Supporting Teens' Academic Needs Daily, PT= parent training, IY= Incredible Years)
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: Type of comparator (tau= treatment as usual, wl= waitlist, PC&S= parent counseling and support, CARE= Coping With ADHD Through Relationships and Education)
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the first arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of parent training interventions, face-to-face and Internet-based, this variable would be set to f2f and Internet, respectively.
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the second arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of control groups, waitlist and placebo, this variable would be set to wl and plac, respectively. Typically, multiarm trials employ two or more active treatments (e.g. CBT and problem-solving therapy), which are compared to the same control group (e.g. a waitlist). This means that values in multi_arm2 do not differ (e.g. they are always wl for this specific multiarm trial); nevertheless, the variable should be specified in the dataset.
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: Describes the instrument through which the relevant outcome was measured.
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: Encodes how the outcome measurement was rated (e.g., parent, teacher, mother, coder).
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_category: Broad behavioural outcome category (ADHD total= total ADHD score, ADHD HI= hiperactivity, ADHD A= inattention, behavioural problems= other behavioural problems).
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: Type of outcome that builds the basis of the comparison, e.g. means and standard deviations (msd), change from baseline, response, remission, other statistics, etc.
metadata/variable_description.json.Source of participants: Encodes how the participants were recruited (e.g., community, clinic, school).
metadata/variable_description.json.Country: Country where the trial was carried out
metadata/variable_description.json.time: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (e.g. post or follow-up).
metadata/variable_description.json.time_weeks: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained, in weeks after randomization. If unspecified, code as NA.
metadata/variable_description.json.seq_gen: Score on the sequence generation scale of the Risk of Bias assessment (0= high risk; 1= low risk; ?= unclear).
metadata/variable_description.json.alloc_conce: Score on the allocation concealment scale of the Risk of Bias assessment (0= high risk; 1= low risk; ?= unclear).
metadata/variable_description.json.blindind_assess: Score on the blinding of assessors scale of the Risk of Bias assessment (0= high risk; 1= low risk; ?= unclear).
metadata/variable_description.json.missing_data: Score on the dealing with missing data scale of the Risk of Bias assessment (0= high risk; 1= low risk; ?= unclear).
metadata/variable_description.json.vested_int: Score on the vested interest scale of the Risk of Bias assessment (0= high risk; 1= low risk; ?= unclear).
metadata/variable_description.json.selec_report: Score on the selective reporting scale of the Risk of Bias assessment (0= high risk; 1= low risk; ?= unclear).
metadata/variable_description.json.d1: Risk of bias (tool 2) domain 1: Randomization process (low, some concerns or high)
metadata/variable_description.json.d2: Risk of bias (tool 2) domain 2: Deviations from the intended interventions (low, some concerns or high)
metadata/variable_description.json.d3: Risk of bias (tool 2) domain 3: Missing outcome data (low, some concerns or high)
metadata/variable_description.json.d4: Risk of bias (tool 2) domain 4: Measurement of the outcome (low, some concerns or high)
metadata/variable_description.json.d5: Risk of bias (tool 2) domain 5: Selection of the reported result (low, some concerns or high)
metadata/variable_description.json.rob: Overall risk of bias score (low, some concerns or high)
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm1: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm2: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm1: Total number of participants arm 1 (event data)
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm2: Total number of participants arm 2 (event data)
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm1: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm2: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_g: The pre-calculated value of Hedges' g (small-sample bias corrected standardized mean difference; Hedges, 1981).
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr: The pre-calculated value of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr_se: The standard error of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json..id: metapsyTools generated variable: Unique identifier for a trial arm comparison/row.
metadata/variable_description.json..g: metapsyTools generated variable: Calculated effect size (Hedges' g).
metadata/variable_description.json..g_se: metapsyTools generated variable: Standard error of Hedges' g.
metadata/variable_description.json..log_rr: metapsyTools generated variable: Calculated effect size (logeRR).
metadata/variable_description.json..log_rr_se: metapsyTools generated variable: Standard error of logeRR.
metadata/variable_description.json..event_arm1: metapsyTools generated variable: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm.
metadata/variable_description.json..event_arm2: metapsyTools generated variable: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm.
metadata/variable_description.json..totaln_arm1: metapsyTools generated variable: Total sample size in the first trial arm.
metadata/variable_description.json..totaln_arm2: metapsyTools generated variable: Total sample size in the second trial arm.

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-psychosis-psyctr: Version 26.0.2
metadata.description:
The data-psychosis-psyctr dataset 📊

The data-psychosis-psyctr dataset is a meta-analytic research domain MARD which is part of the Metapsy project. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of randomized trials on psychological interventions for schizophrenia and psychosis. The date of the last search update is provided here. More details about a larger version of this dataset can be accessed in the published network meta-analysis.

This dataset includes psychological interventions vs. control (psy vs ctr) comparisons. Effect sizes are provided for three types of outcomes at post-test: total symptoms, negative symptoms, and positive symptoms. It includes one type of effect size calculation per study, giving priority to change scores, followed by means and standard deviations at post-test.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.

inclusion: Adults aged 18-65 years of all sexes

Participants diagnosed with schizophrenia or a related psychotic disorder (schizophreniform disorder, schizoaffective disorder, delusional disorder), including first-episode psychosis, drug-resistant symptoms, and participants receiving concurrent treatment as usual and/or pharmacotherapy
exclusion: Trials targeting young or older adults specifically (e.g., upper age limit below 40 or lower age limit above 40)
Trials in which participants with a diagnosis of bipolar disorder, substance-induced psychosis, postpartum psychosis, or dementia accounted for more than 10% of the sample
Trials in which participants were recruited from specific populations (e.g., veterans, forensic settings) accounted for more than 50% of the sample
Trials in which participants had a comorbid serious medical illness or other psychiatric disorders (except anxiety or depression)
Trials with participants at ultra/high risk of developing a psychotic disorder (e.g., attenuated psychotic symptoms, brief limited intermittent psychotic symptoms)
Trials targeting participants with primary negative symptoms

inclusion: Psychological interventions that are theory-driven, goal-oriented, and aimed at reducing psychotic symptoms and improving functioning (e.g., cognitive-behavioral therapy for psychosis [CBTp], social skills training, family-based interventions, mindfulness-based interventions, metacognitive training, cognitive remediation)
Interventions delivered in individual, group, computer-based, (semi-)guided online, or blended formats
exclusion: Trials comparing two types of psychological interventions (e.g., CBTp vs metacognitive training) or trials comparing variations of the same intervention (e.g., three vs six months of CBTp)
Trials with art, music, physical exercise, animal-assisted, medication-only, or alternative-medicine interventions

Interventions focused on vocational programs or delivered within service-wide interventions, unless both groups received the same enhanced service differing only by the specific psychological intervention
Family-based interventions in which the person with psychosis was not included
Psychoeducation-based interventions without an active treatment component (e.g., medication-adherence only)
Trials without the involvement of a therapist (e.g., non-guided online interventions, cognitive remediation with only computerized training sets)
Trials in which the intervention lasts longer than 12 months
Behavioral interventions that would now be considered unethical (e.g., self-shock)

inclusion: Waitlist control
Befriending
Non-specific supportive counseling
Non-specific psychoeducation

Treatment as usual (TAU), categorised into four levels: TAU0 (medication only with no follow-up); TAU1 (medication with routine check-up appointments or follow-up); TAU2 (case management and/or access to multidisciplinary team services such as social work, occupational therapy, and psychosocial interventions); TAU3 (TAU2 plus specified psychological interventions such as CBT). When TAU was not described, the country of the trial (psychiatrists per 100,000 population, per WHO Global Health Observatory) and its publication year were used to impute the likely TAU level
Total, positive, and/or negative scores on the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS; Kay, 1987)
Total, positive, and/or negative scores on the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS; Overall, 1962)
Negative-symptom scores on the Scale for the Assessment of Negative Symptoms (SANS; Andreasen, 1984)
Positive-symptom scores on the Scale for the Assessment of Positive Symptoms (SAPS; Andreasen, 1984)
Other established clinical scales measuring total, positive, and/or negative psychotic symptoms (e.g., CPRS, BNSS, CAINS)
exclusion: Symptom outcomes reported using a subscale of an instrument (e.g., SAPS Delusions Subscale)
Symptom outcomes other than total, positive, and/or negative scores (e.g., PSYRATS hallucinations and delusions scores)
Outcome data other than psychotic symptoms (e.g., functioning, weight management, relapse prevention)

inclusion: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs); given the nature of psychological interventions, open-label RCTs (for both participants and the person delivering the intervention) are included
Cluster RCTs (in which groups of participants, e.g., hospitals, are randomly assigned to study arms rather than individual participants)
exclusion: Non-randomized trials (e.g., case series)
Quasi-randomized trials (e.g., allocation by date of birth)
Crossover RCTs (in which participants receive different treatments in sequence)

metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm1: ALL - Protocol with 4 psychotherapies combined; CBT -Cognitive behaviour therapy; CR - Cognitive remediation; CRSS - Cognitive remediation focussed on social cognition; EMDR - Eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing; FT - Family therapy; HIT - Hallucinations focused integrative therapy; MCT - Metacognitive therapy; MPE - Mindfulness-based psychoeducation; PE – Psychoeducation;  SST - Social skills training;  WB – Wellbeing
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: Type of comparator (TAU0= Minimal contact and/or intervention- for example, medication only with no follow up, TAU1= Medication with routine check-up appointments/follow up,  TAU2=  Case management and/or access to MDT services such as social work, OT and psychosocial interventions, TAU3 = TAU2 plus specified delivered psychological interventions, for example, CBT or motivational interviewing, BF= befriending, CCBF= computerised contorl befirending, CC= computerised control, SC= supportive counceling, OT= occupational therapy, CAT= cognitive adaptive therapy)
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the first arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of CBT interventions, face-to-face and Internet-based, this variable would be set to f2f and Internet, respectively
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the second arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of control groups, waitlist and placebo, this variable would be set to wl and plac, respectively. Typically, multiarm trials employ two or more active treatments (e.g., CBT and problem-solving therapy), which are compared to the same control group (e.g., a waitlist). This means that values in multi_arm2 do not differ (e.g., they are always wl for this specific multiarm trial); nevertheless, the variable should be specified in the dataset
metadata/variable_description.json.comparison: Comparison between the trial arms, psy= psychotherapy, and ctr= control
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: The msd factor level is typically used for the post-intervention outcomes expressed in means and standard deviations. The change is reported when available
metadata/variable_description.json.symptom_domain: Domain of the psychotic symptom measured with a specific instrument used in a trial (i.e., positive symptoms, negative symptoms, and total symptoms)
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: This variable describes the instrument through which the relevant outcome was measured in combination with the symptom domain measured with that instrument
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: This variable encodes if the measured outcome was clinician-rated ('interviewer-rated') or caregiver-rated ('caregiver-rated')
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm1: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm2: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm1: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm2: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm1: Total number of participants arm 1 (event data)
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm2: Total number of participants arm 2 (event data)
metadata/variable_description.json.N_randomized_total: Total number of randomized participants in the trial
metadata/variable_description.json.time: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (e.g., post or follow-up)
metadata/variable_description.json.time_weeks: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained, in weeks after randomization (set to NA if this information was not available)
metadata/variable_description.json.trial_length: Total length of the trial in weeks
metadata/variable_description.json.format: Format of the intervention (i.e., individual, group, computer based an mixed)
metadata/variable_description.json.n_sessions_arm1: Total number of sessions in arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.n_sessions_arm2: Total number of sessions in arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.country: Exact country where the study was conducted
metadata/variable_description.json.recruitment: Inpatient; Outpatient; Both inpatient and outpatient
metadata/variable_description.json.diagnosis: Inclusion diagnostic criteria
metadata/variable_description.json.dur_ill_arm1: Mean duration of the illness in years in arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.Domain 5; selection of the reported resu: Domain 5 - Selection of the reported result
metadata/variable_description.json.rob: Overall risk of bias rating (low risk=0, some concern=1, high risk=2)
metadata/variable_description.json..id: MetapsyTools generated variable: Unique identifier for a trial arm comparison/row
metadata/variable_description.json..g: MetapsyTools generated variable: Calculated effect size (Hedges' g)
metadata/variable_description.json..g_se: MetapsyTools generated variable: Standard error of Hedges' g

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-psychosis-psyctr: Version 26.0.1
metadata.description:
The data-psychosis-psyctr dataset 📊

The data-psychosis-psyctr dataset is a meta-analytic research domain MARD which is part of the Metapsy project. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of randomized trials on psychological interventions for schizophrenia and psychosis. The date of the last search update is provided here. More details about a larger version of this dataset can be accessed in the published network meta-analysis.

This dataset includes psychological interventions vs. control (psy vs ctr) comparisons. Effect sizes are provided for three types of outcomes at post-test: total symptoms, negative symptoms, and positive symptoms. It includes one type of effect size calculation per study, giving priority to change scores, followed by means and standard deviations at post-test.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.

metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm1: ALL - Protocol with 4 psychotherapies combined; CBT -Cognitive behaviour therapy; CR - Cognitive remediation; CRSS - Cognitive remediation focussed on social cognition; EMDR - Eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing; FT - Family therapy; HIT - Hallucinations focused integrative therapy; MCT - Metacognitive therapy; MPE - Mindfulness-based psychoeducation; PE – Psychoeducation;  SST - Social skills training;  WB – Wellbeing
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: Type of comparator (TAU0= Minimal contact and/or intervention- for example, medication only with no follow up, TAU1= Medication with routine check-up appointments/follow up,  TAU2=  Case management and/or access to MDT services such as social work, OT and psychosocial interventions, TAU3 = TAU2 plus specified delivered psychological interventions, for example, CBT or motivational interviewing, BF= befriending, CCBF= computerised contorl befirending, CC= computerised control, SC= supportive counceling, OT= occupational therapy, CAT= cognitive adaptive therapy)
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the first arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of CBT interventions, face-to-face and Internet-based, this variable would be set to f2f and Internet, respectively
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the second arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of control groups, waitlist and placebo, this variable would be set to wl and plac, respectively. Typically, multiarm trials employ two or more active treatments (e.g., CBT and problem-solving therapy), which are compared to the same control group (e.g., a waitlist). This means that values in multi_arm2 do not differ (e.g., they are always wl for this specific multiarm trial); nevertheless, the variable should be specified in the dataset
metadata/variable_description.json.comparison: Comparison between the trial arms, psy= psychotherapy, and ctr= control
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: The msd factor level is typically used for the post-intervention outcomes expressed in means and standard deviations. The change is reported when available
metadata/variable_description.json.symptom_domain: Domain of the psychotic symptom measured with a specific instrument used in a trial (i.e., positive symptoms, negative symptoms, and total symptoms)
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: This variable describes the instrument through which the relevant outcome was measured in combination with the symptom domain measured with that instrument
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: This variable encodes if the measured outcome was clinician-rated ('interviewer-rated') or caregiver-rated ('caregiver-rated')
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm1: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm2: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm1: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm2: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm1: Total number of participants arm 1 (event data)
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm2: Total number of participants arm 2 (event data)
metadata/variable_description.json.N_randomized_total: Total number of randomized participants in the trial
metadata/variable_description.json.time: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (e.g., post or follow-up)
metadata/variable_description.json.time_weeks: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained, in weeks after randomization (set to NA if this information was not available)
metadata/variable_description.json.trial_length: Total length of the trial in weeks
metadata/variable_description.json.format: Format of the intervention (i.e., individual, group, computer based an mixed)
metadata/variable_description.json.n_sessions_arm1: Total number of sessions in arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.n_sessions_arm2: Total number of sessions in arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.country: Exact country where the study was conducted
metadata/variable_description.json.recruitment: Inpatient; Outpatient; Both inpatient and outpatient
metadata/variable_description.json.diagnosis: Inclusion diagnostic criteria
metadata/variable_description.json.dur_ill_arm1: Mean duration of the illness in years in arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.Domain 5; selection of the reported resu: Domain 5 - Selection of the reported result
metadata/variable_description.json.rob: Overall risk of bias rating (low risk=0, some concern=1, high risk=2)
metadata/variable_description.json..id: MetapsyTools generated variable: Unique identifier for a trial arm comparison/row
metadata/variable_description.json..g: MetapsyTools generated variable: Calculated effect size (Hedges' g)
metadata/variable_description.json..g_se: MetapsyTools generated variable: Standard error of Hedges' g

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-psychosis-psyctr: Version 26.0.0
metadata.description:
The data-psychosis-psyctr dataset 📊

The data-psychosis-psyctr dataset is a meta-analytic research domain MARD which is part of the Metapsy project. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of randomized trials on psychological interventions for schizophrenia and psychosis. The date of the last search update is provided here. More details about a larger version of this dataset can be accessed in the published network meta-analysis.

This dataset includes psychological interventions vs. control (psy vs ctr) comparisons. Effect sizes are provided for three types of outcomes at post-test: total symptoms, negative symptoms, and positive symptoms. It includes one type of effect size calculation per study, giving priority to change scores, followed by means and standard deviations at post-test.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-ed-digital-psyctr: Version 26.0.2
metadata.description:
The data-ed-digital-psyctr dataset 📊

The data-ed-digital-psyctr dataset is part of the meta-analytic research domain (MARD) on psychotherapy for eating disorders. This MARD is part of the Metapsy project. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of trials on digital interventions for eating disorders. The date of the last search update is provided here.

This dataset includes psychotherapy vs. control (psy vs ctr) comparisons. Effect sizes are provided for eating disorder psychopathology, objective binge eating frequency, compensatory behaviours, abstinence, shape/ weight concerns, dietary restraint, eating concerns, depression, anxiety, clinical impairment, quality of life/ well-being, general distress, and self-esteem at post-test and follow-up. It includes one type of effect size calculation per study, giving priority to means and standard deviations at post-test, followed by change scores, binary outcomes, and other statistics.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.

inclusion: participants pre-selected for elevated eating disorder symptoms, as established through either a formal diagnostic interview confirming a threshold or subthreshold diagnosis, scores above a validated cutoff on a standardized rating scale, or endorsement of eating disorder behaviors (eg, >=3 objective binge episodes)
exclusion: Unselected samples, or those screened solely for risk factors (eg, weight concerns) without the presence of eating disorder symptoms

inclusion: Digital interventions for eating disorders (defined as interventions delivered via a computer, mobile phone, or tablet, where the means of delivery included the internet, downloadable software, CD-ROM, smartphone application, or chatbot; professional or peer support was permitted)
exclusion: therapist-led treatments delivered via online means (eg, video conferencing and so on), cognitive training programs, blended treatments, and relapse prevention programs

inclusion: control group (waiting list, usual care, placebo, educational resources, or other nontherapeutic material)
Randomized controlled trials
published and unpublished studies

metadata/variable_description.json.study: Unique study identifier, typically first author and publication year.
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm1: Description of the intervention condition.
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: Description of the comparison condition.
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: Indicator identifying intervention arms originating from the same multi-arm trial.
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: Indicator identifying comparison arms originating from the same multi-arm trial.
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: Type of outcome analysed (e.g., continuous or dichotomous).
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: Outcome measure or instrument used to assess the construct.
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: Direction of scoring for the outcome measure (higher or lower scores indicating greater symptom severity).
metadata/variable_description.json.construct: Outcome construct assessed (e.g., eating disorder psychopathology, binge eating frequency, body dissatisfaction).
metadata/variable_description.json.time_weeks: Time from baseline to assessment, expressed in weeks.
metadata/variable_description.json.time: Assessment time point (e.g., post-treatment, first follow-up, last follow-up).
metadata/variable_description.json.mean_arm1: Mean outcome value for the intervention group.
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_arm1: Standard deviation of the intervention group.
metadata/variable_description.json.n_arm1: Sample size contributing data for the intervention group.
metadata/variable_description.json.mean_arm2: Mean outcome value for the comparison group.
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_arm2: Standard deviation of the comparison group.
metadata/variable_description.json.n_arm2: Sample size contributing data for the comparison group.
metadata/variable_description.json.mean_change_arm1: Mean change from baseline for the intervention group.
metadata/variable_description.json.mean_change_arm2: Mean change from baseline for the comparison group.
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm1: Standard deviation of the change scores for the intervention group.
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm2: Standard deviation of the change scores for the comparison group.
metadata/variable_description.json.n_change_arm1: Sample size contributing change score data for the intervention group.
metadata/variable_description.json.n_change_arm2: Sample size contributing change score data for the comparison group.
metadata/variable_description.json.dich_paper: Indicator that the study reported dichotomous outcome data.
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm1: Number of participants experiencing the event in the intervention group.
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm2: Number of participants experiencing the event in the comparison group.
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm1: Total number of participants included in the dichotomous analysis for the intervention group.
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm2: Total number of participants included in the dichotomous analysis for the comparison group.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_g: Pre-calculated Hedges' g effect size reported by the study or derived during data extraction.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_g_se: Standard error of the pre-calculated Hedges' g.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr: Pre-calculated log risk ratio.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr_se: Standard error of the pre-calculated log risk ratio.

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-ed-digital-psyctr: 26.0.1
metadata.description:
The data-ed-digital-psyctr dataset 📊

The data-ed-digital-psyctr dataset is part of the meta-analytic research domain (MARD) on psychotherapy for eating disorders. This MARD is part of the Metapsy project. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of trials on digital interventions for eating disorders. The date of the last search update is provided here.

This dataset includes psychotherapy vs. control (psy vs ctr) comparisons. Effect sizes are provided for eating disorder psychopathology, objective binge eating frequency, compensatory behaviours, abstinence, shape/ weight concerns, dietary restraint, eating concerns, depression, anxiety, clinical impairment, quality of life/ well-being, general distress, and self-esteem at post-test and follow-up. It includes one type of effect size calculation per study, giving priority to means and standard deviations at post-test, followed by change scores, binary outcomes, and other statistics.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.

inclusion: participants pre-selected for elevated eating disorder symptoms, as established through either a formal diagnostic interview confirming a threshold or subthreshold diagnosis, scores above a validated cutoff on a standardized rating scale, or endorsement of eating disorder behaviors (eg, >=3 objective binge episodes)
exclusion: Unselected samples, or those screened solely for risk factors (eg, weight concerns) without the presence of eating disorder symptoms

inclusion: Digital interventions for eating disorders (defined as interventions delivered via a computer, mobile phone, or tablet, where the means of delivery included the internet, downloadable software, CD-ROM, smartphone application, or chatbot; professional or peer support was permitted)
exclusion: therapist-led treatments delivered via online means (eg, video conferencing and so on), cognitive training programs, blended treatments, and relapse prevention programs

inclusion: control group (waiting list, usual care, placebo, educational resources, or other nontherapeutic material)
Randomized controlled trials
published and unpublished studies

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-depression-psiloctr: Version 26.0.0
metadata.description:
The data-depression-psiloctr dataset 📊

The data-depression-psiloctr dataset is a meta-analytic research domain (MARD) on psilocybin-assisted therapies for adults with depressive symptoms. This MARD is part of the Metapsy project. The date of the last search update is provided here. This dataset includes psilocybin-assisted therapy vs. control ('psy vs ctr') comparisons. Effect sizes are provided for outcomes at post-test and long-term follow-ups, if available.

This living database has been developed by the Sypres (Synthesis of Psychedelic Research Studies) Collaboration. Further information on Sypres and its underlying methodology can be found in this published article.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard. All included information has been independently extracted two researchers. Risk of bias ratings were conducted using the Cochrane Collaboration Risk of Bias Tool (Version 2).

metadata/variable_description.json.study: Author of the study and year of publication

metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: condition in the second arm (psil = psilocybin, wl = waitlist control, ncn = niacin,pcb = placebo, mbsr = mindfulness-based stress reduction)
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: distinguishes arms in multi-arm studies (e.g. dose of psilocybin)
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: distinguishes arms in multi-arm studies (e.g. dose of psilocybin)
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: how the outcome is reported (change = change from baseline score, msd = endpoint mean and standard deviation, response = response (dichotomous outcome), remission = remission (dichotomous outcome), imsd = imputed endpoint mean and standard deviation (calculated for studies initially reported only as change from baseline)
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: depression instrument used to measure outcome
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: describes who administers or completes the depression instrument (clinician = clinician-rated scale, self-report = self-report scale)
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument_symptom: describes the symptom the instrument surveys (depression)
metadata/variable_description.json.primary_instrument: describes if the instrument listed was reported as or chosen as the primary outcome instrument (1 = yes, 0 = no)
metadata/variable_description.json.cov_time_point: timepoint at which the outcome measure was taken according to Covidence data extraction template timepoint
metadata/variable_description.json.time: timepoint at which the outcome measure was taken as reported in the paper and listed in Covidence
metadata/variable_description.json.time_days: timepoint at which the outcome measure was taken in days, relative to baseline
metadata/variable_description.json.time_weeks: timepoint at which the outcome measure was taken in weeks, relative to baseline

metadata/variable_description.json.post_crossover: describes if the timepoint listed corresponds to a time before crossover or after crossover (0 = before crossover, 1 = after crossover, NA = does not correspond to a crossover study design

metadata/variable_description.json.mean_arm1: mean value in arm 1 (for endpoint studies)

metadata/variable_description.json.cumulative_dose_arm2: cumulative dose of drug used in the second arm (taking into account mg from prior dosing session). Does not include dosing sessions after crossover for post-crossover timepoints.
metadata/variable_description.json.dose_days: amount of time since the most recent dose, in days
metadata/variable_description.json.dose_weeks: amount of time since the most recent dose, in weeks
metadata/variable_description.json.mean_age: mean age of study participants at baseline
metadata/variable_description.json.diagnosis: primary diagnosis of study participants (trd = treatment-resistatnt major depressive disorder, mdd = major depressive disorder, dep = depression symptoms without a diagnosis, cancer = cancer, aud = alcohol-use disorder
metadata/variable_description.json.target_group: target group for intervention
metadata/variable_description.json.design: methodological design of the study (crossover = crossover study, paralell = parallel-group study)
metadata/variable_description.json.blinding: specifies whether the study was double-blind or not (open-label = open-label study, double-blind = double-blind study)
metadata/variable_description.json.registration_number: registration number of study in clinical trial registry
metadata/variable_description.json..id: row identification, comprised of study author and year of publication, outcome type, instrument, time, rating, condition_arm1, condition_arm2, multi_arm1, and multi_arm2, separated by underscores
metadata/variable_description.json..g: calculated Hedges' g score (for continuous outcomes)
metadata/variable_description.json..ge_se: calculated standard error of Hedges' g score (for continuous outcomes)
metadata/variable_description.json..log_rr: calculated log risk ratio (for dichotomous outcomes)
metadata/variable_description.json..log_rr_se: calculated standard error of log risk ratio (for dichotomous outcomes)
metadata/variable_description.json..event_arm1: calculated number of events in arm 1 (see event_arm1)
metadata/variable_description.json..event_arm2: calculated number of events in arm 2 (see event_arm2)
metadata/variable_description.json..totaln_arm1: calculated total number of participants in arm 1 (see totaln_arm1)

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-gambling-psyctr: Version 26.0.1
metadata.description:
The data-gambling-psyctr dataset 📊

The data-gambling-psyctr dataset is a meta-analytic research domain MARD) which is part of the Metapsy project. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of randomized trials on psychological interventions for problem gambling and gambling disorder. The date of the last search update is provided here. A published meta-analysis using part of the data from this database can be accessed here.

This dataset includes psychological interventions (CBT, motivational interventions, personalized feedback, etc) vs. control comparisons. Effect sizes are provided for three types of gambling-related outcomes ("gambling_outcome") at post-test and at follow-up: 1) Gambling disorder severity (measured using a variety of measures with some reliability and validity support, including the gambling subscale of the Addiction Severity Index, Gambling Symptom Assessment Scale, the Problem Gambling Severity Index, etc.), 2) Gambling frequency (e.g., number of times gambled), and 3) Gambling intensity (e.g., money spent on gambling), and 4) Gambling duration (e.g., number of hours gambled). Additionally, this dataset also includes data on other outcomes such as anxiety, depression, quality of life, and substance use ("outcome_domain").

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.

extracted_metadata.metadata/search_string.txt:
**PubMed**
---
("intervention"[Title] OR "treat*"[Title] OR "therapy")[Title]) AND ("gambl*"[Title])

**Embase**
---
('intervention':ti OR 'treat*':ti OR 'therapy':ti) AND 'gambl*':ti

**PsycINFO**
---
TI ("intervention" OR "treat*" OR "therapy") AND TI "gambl*"

**Cochrane Reviews & Cochrane Trials**
---
Title abstract keyword ("gambling") AND ("therapy" OR "intervention" OR "treatment")

metadata/variable_description.json.study: Name of first author and year of publication
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm1: Type of treatment (cbt = cognitive-behavioral treatment, mi = motivational intervention, other psy = other psychological treatment, pfi = personalized feedback intervention)
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: Type of comparator (ao = assessment only, cau = care as usual, wl = waitlist)
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the first arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of CBT interventions, face-to-face and Internet-based, this variable would be set to f2f and Internet, respectively. (ind = individual, f2f = face-to-face, grp = group, gsh = guided self-help, ma = Massachusetts, mi = motivational interview, nv = Nevada, ush = unguided self-help, wb = workbook)
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the second arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of control groups, waitlist and placebo, this variable would be set to wl and plac, respectively. Typically, multiarm trials employ two or more active treatments (e.g. CBT and problem-solving therapy), which are compared to the same control group (e.g. a waitlist). This means that values in multi_arm2 do not differ (e.g. they are always wl for this specific multiarm trial); nevertheless, the variable should be specified in the dataset
metadata/variable_description.json..g: metapsyTools generated variable: Calculated effect size (Hedges' g).
metadata/variable_description.json..g_se: metapsyTools generated variable: Standard error of Hedges' g.
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: This variable encodes the type of outcome that builds the basis of the comparison, e.g. means and standard deviations (msd), mean difference (md)
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_domain: This variable includes domains of outcomes (anxiety = anxiety, depression = depression, gambling = gambling, su = substance use)
metadata/variable_description.json.gambling_outcome: This variable specifies the type of gambling outcome measured: Gambling disorder severity (measured using a variety of measures with some reliability and validity support, including the gambling subscale of the Addiction Severity Index, Gambling Symptom Assessment Scale, the Problem Gambling Severity Index, etc.), Gambling frequency (e.g., number of times gambled), and Gambling intensity (e.g., money spent on gambling), and Gambling duration (e.g., number of hours gambled)
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: This variable describes the outcome that was measured (frequency = number of days gambled, intensity = amount of money gambled, duration = amount of time gambled, dsm-iii = DSM-III criteria for pathological gambling, dsm-iv = DSM-IV criteria for pathological gambling, dsm-5 = DSM-5 criteria for gambling disorder, asi = Addiction Severity Index-Gambling, audit = Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test, bai = Beck Anxiety Inventory, bdi-2 = Beck Depression Inventory-2, cpgi = Canadian Problem Gambling Index, dd = daily diary, dass = Depression and Anxiety Stress Scale total score, dass-a = Depression and Anxiety Stress Scale Anxiety score, dass-d = Depression and Anxiety Stress Scale Depression score, dgd = alcoholic drinks per gambling day, global = global estimate; gsas = Gambling Symptom Assessment Scale, hads-a = Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale Anxiety score, hads-d = Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale Depression score, has = Hamilton Anxiety Scale, hrsd = Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression, igd = intoxicated gambling days, nods = National Opinion Research Center DSM Screen for Gambling Problems, pgsi = Problem Gambling Severity Index, player = player data from real-world gaming operators, qoli = Quality of Life Inventory, sghs = Short Gambling Harm Screen, sogs = South Oaks Gambling Screen, stai-s = State Trait Anxiety Inventory state score, stai-t = State Trait Anxiety Inventory trait score, swlq = Satisfaction with Life Questionnaire, tlfb = Timeline Followback, whoqol = World Health Organisation Quality of Life, ybocs = Yale–Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale Modified for Pathological Gambling)
metadata/variable_description.json.time: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (e.g. post or follow-up).
metadata/variable_description.json.time_weeks: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (set to NA if this information was not available). For posttreatment outcomes, time is measured in weeks after randomization. For follow up outcomes, time is measured in weeks after treatment termination.
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm1: Standard deviation arm 1 at baseline
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_sd_arm2: Number of participants arm 1 at baseline
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm2: Number of participants arm 2 at baseline
metadata/variable_description.json.format: ind= individual; grp= group; comb = combined individual and group treatment
metadata/variable_description.json.format_details: It includes more details about the format, when necessary (gsh= guided self-help; ush= unguided self-help)
metadata/variable_description.json.country: us= USA; uk= United Kingdom; eu= Europe; can= Canada; au= australia; eas= east asia; oth= other
metadata/variable_description.json.recruitment: Clinical = clinical sample; Com = includes helpline and community advertisements
metadata/variable_description.json.diagnosis: The diagnosis of participants included in the trial. gd = gambling disorder confirmed by clinical interview; perc = perception of a gambling problem or subjective need for help; sub = problem gambling (i.e., subclinical symptoms)
metadata/variable_description.json.screen: The type of assessment used to determine participants’ eligibility in the study. ci = clinical interview; perc = perception of a gambling problem or subjective need for help; cut = cut score on a validated assessment tool
metadata/variable_description.json.rob_domain1: Randomization sequence (Low = low risk; High = high risk; Some concerns = some concerns)
metadata/variable_description.json.rob_domain2: Intervention deviations (Low = low risk; High = high risk; Some concerns = some concerns)
metadata/variable_description.json.rob_domain3: Missing data (Low = low risk; High = high risk; Some concerns = some concerns)
metadata/variable_description.json.rob_domain4: Outcome measurement (Low = low risk; High = high risk; Some concerns = some concerns)
metadata/variable_description.json.rob_domain5: Selection of results (Low = low risk; High = high risk; Some concerns = some concerns)
metadata/variable_description.json.rob: Overall risk of bias score (Low = low risk; High = high risk; Some concerns = some concerns)
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: metapsytools standard variable
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm1: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm2: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm1: Total number of participants arm 1 (event data)
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm2: Total number of participants arm 2 (event data)
metadata/variable_description.json..id: metapsyTools generated variable: Unique identifier for a trial arm comparison/row.

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-gambling-psyctr: Version 26.0.0
metadata.description:
The data-gambling-psyctr dataset 📊

The data-gambling-psyctr dataset is a meta-analytic research domain MARD) which is part of the Metapsy project. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of randomized trials on psychological interventions for problem gambling and gambling disorder. The date of the last search update is provided here. A published meta-analysis using part of the data from this database can be accessed here.

This dataset includes psychological interventions (CBT, motivational interventions, personalized feedback, etc) vs. control comparisons. Effect sizes are provided for three types of gambling-related outcomes ("gambling_outcome") at post-test and at follow-up: 1) Gambling disorder severity (measured using a variety of measures with some reliability and validity support, including the gambling subscale of the Addiction Severity Index, Gambling Symptom Assessment Scale, the Problem Gambling Severity Index, etc.), 2) Gambling frequency (e.g., number of times gambled), and 3) Gambling intensity (e.g., money spent on gambling), and 4) Gambling duration (e.g., number of hours gambled). Additionally, this dataset also includes data on other outcomes such as anxiety, depression, quality of life, and substance use ("outcome_domain").

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.

metadata/variable_description.json.study: Name of first author and year of publication
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm1: Type of treatment (cbt = cognitive-behavioral treatment, mi = motivational intervention, other psy = other psychological treatment, pfi = personalized feedback intervention)
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: Type of comparator (ao = assessment only, cau = care as usual, wl = waitlist)
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the first arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of CBT interventions, face-to-face and Internet-based, this variable would be set to f2f and Internet, respectively. (ind = individual, f2f = face-to-face, grp = group, gsh = guided self-help, ma = Massachusetts, mi = motivational interview, nv = Nevada, ush = unguided self-help, wb = workbook)
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the second arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of control groups, waitlist and placebo, this variable would be set to wl and plac, respectively. Typically, multiarm trials employ two or more active treatments (e.g. CBT and problem-solving therapy), which are compared to the same control group (e.g. a waitlist). This means that values in multi_arm2 do not differ (e.g. they are always wl for this specific multiarm trial); nevertheless, the variable should be specified in the dataset
metadata/variable_description.json..g: metapsyTools generated variable: Calculated effect size (Hedges' g).
metadata/variable_description.json..g_se: metapsyTools generated variable: Standard error of Hedges' g.
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: This variable encodes the type of outcome that builds the basis of the comparison, e.g. means and standard deviations (msd), mean difference (md)
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_domain: This variable includes domains of outcomes (anxiety = anxiety, depression = depression, gambling = gambling, su = substance use)
metadata/variable_description.json.gambling_outcome: This variable specifies the type of gambling outcome measured: Gambling disorder severity (measured using a variety of measures with some reliability and validity support, including the gambling subscale of the Addiction Severity Index, Gambling Symptom Assessment Scale, the Problem Gambling Severity Index, etc.), Gambling frequency (e.g., number of times gambled), and Gambling intensity (e.g., money spent on gambling), and Gambling duration (e.g., number of hours gambled)
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: This variable describes the outcome that was measured (frequency = number of days gambled, intensity = amount of money gambled, duration = amount of time gambled, dsm-iii = DSM-III criteria for pathological gambling, dsm-iv = DSM-IV criteria for pathological gambling, dsm-5 = DSM-5 criteria for gambling disorder, asi = Addiction Severity Index-Gambling, audit = Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test, bai = Beck Anxiety Inventory, bdi-2 = Beck Depression Inventory-2, cpgi = Canadian Problem Gambling Index, dd = daily diary, dass = Depression and Anxiety Stress Scale total score, dass-a = Depression and Anxiety Stress Scale Anxiety score, dass-d = Depression and Anxiety Stress Scale Depression score, dgd = alcoholic drinks per gambling day, global = global estimate; gsas = Gambling Symptom Assessment Scale, hads-a = Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale Anxiety score, hads-d = Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale Depression score, has = Hamilton Anxiety Scale, hrsd = Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression, igd = intoxicated gambling days, nods = National Opinion Research Center DSM Screen for Gambling Problems, pgsi = Problem Gambling Severity Index, player = player data from real-world gaming operators, qoli = Quality of Life Inventory, sghs = Short Gambling Harm Screen, sogs = South Oaks Gambling Screen, stai-s = State Trait Anxiety Inventory state score, stai-t = State Trait Anxiety Inventory trait score, swlq = Satisfaction with Life Questionnaire, tlfb = Timeline Followback, whoqol = World Health Organisation Quality of Life, ybocs = Yale–Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale Modified for Pathological Gambling)
metadata/variable_description.json.time: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (e.g. post or follow-up).
metadata/variable_description.json.time_weeks: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (set to NA if this information was not available). For posttreatment outcomes, time is measured in weeks after randomization. For follow up outcomes, time is measured in weeks after treatment termination.
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm1: Standard deviation arm 1 at baseline
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_sd_arm2: Number of participants arm 1 at baseline
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm2: Number of participants arm 2 at baseline
metadata/variable_description.json.format: ind= individual; grp= group; comb = combined individual and group treatment
metadata/variable_description.json.format_details: It includes more details about the format, when necessary (gsh= guided self-help; ush= unguided self-help)
metadata/variable_description.json.country: us= USA; uk= United Kingdom; eu= Europe; can= Canada; au= australia; eas= east asia; oth= other
metadata/variable_description.json.recruitment: Clinical = clinical sample; Com = includes helpline and community advertisements
metadata/variable_description.json.diagnosis: The diagnosis of participants included in the trial. gd = gambling disorder confirmed by clinical interview; perc = perception of a gambling problem or subjective need for help; sub = problem gambling (i.e., subclinical symptoms)
metadata/variable_description.json.screen: The type of assessment used to determine participants’ eligibility in the study. ci = clinical interview; perc = perception of a gambling problem or subjective need for help; cut = cut score on a validated assessment tool
metadata/variable_description.json.rob_domain1: Randomization sequence (Low = low risk; High = high risk; Some concerns = some concerns)
metadata/variable_description.json.rob_domain2: Intervention deviations (Low = low risk; High = high risk; Some concerns = some concerns)
metadata/variable_description.json.rob_domain3: Missing data (Low = low risk; High = high risk; Some concerns = some concerns)
metadata/variable_description.json.rob_domain4: Outcome measurement (Low = low risk; High = high risk; Some concerns = some concerns)
metadata/variable_description.json.rob_domain5: Selection of results (Low = low risk; High = high risk; Some concerns = some concerns)
metadata/variable_description.json.rob: Overall risk of bias score (Low = low risk; High = high risk; Some concerns = some concerns)
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: metapsytools standard variable
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm1: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm2: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm1: Total number of participants arm 1 (event data)
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm2: Total number of participants arm 2 (event data)

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-ptsd-mdmactr: Version 26.0.1
metadata.description:
The data-ptsd-mdmactr dataset 📊

The data-ptsd-mdmactr dataset is a meta-analytic research domain (MARD) on MDMA therapies for adults with post-traumatic stress disorder. This MARD is part of the Metapsy project. The date of the last search update is provided here. This dataset includes MDMA therapy vs. control ('mdma vs ctr') comparisons. Effect sizes are provided for outcomes at post-test and long-term follow-ups, if available.

This living database has been developed by the Sypres (Synthesis of Psychedelic Research Studies) Collaboration. Further information on Sypres and its underlying methodology can be found in this published article.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard. All included information has been independently extracted two researchers. Risk of bias ratings were conducted using the Cochrane Collaboration Risk of Bias Tool (Version 2).

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-bodily-distress-psyctr: Version 25.1.0
metadata.description:
The data-bodily-distress-psyctr dataset 📊

<img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/DOI-10.5281%2Fzenodo.17405019-blue">

The data-bodily-distress-psyctr dataset is based on a network meta-analysis on cognitive behavioral interventions and acceptance- and mindfulness-based interventions for adults with bodily distress. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of randomized controlled trials that report the effect of cognitive behavioral as well as acceptance- and mindfulness-based interventions on somatic symptom severity, depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, health anxiety, and perceived health status. The dataset also contains information about negative effects and treatment satisfaction. This dataset includes psychotherapy versus control (psy vs ctr) comparisons. The date of the last search update is provided here. The results of the network meta-analysis can be found in this published article.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard. All included information has been independently extracted by two researchers. Risk of bias ratings were conducted using the Cochrane Collaboration Risk of Bias Tool 2 (RoB 2). Re-ratings using the Metapsy Risk of Bias tool are currently ongoing.

metadata/variable_description.json.author: [author(s)] et al., [year]
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm1: Condition in the first trial arm. The condition name is standardized to ensure comparability across trials (e.g. cbt for all trial arms that employed cognitive-behavioral psychotherapy).
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: Condition in the second trial arm. The condition name is standardized to ensure comparability across trials (e.g. wlc for all trial arms that employed a waitlist control group).
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the first arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of CBT interventions, face-to-face and Internet-based, this variable would be set to f2f and Internet, respectively.
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the second arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of control groups, waitlist and placebo, this variable would be set to wl and plac, respectively. Typically, multiarm trials employ two or more active treatments (e.g. CBT and problem-solving therapy), which are compared to the same control group (e.g. a waitlist). This means that values in multi_arm2 do not differ (e.g. they are always wl for this specific multiarm trial); nevertheless, the variable should be specified in the dataset.
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome: This variable encodes the measured outcome: somatic symptoms (som), depression (depr), anxiety (anx), perceived health status (phs), health anxiety (ha)
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: This variable encodes the type of outcome that builds the basis of the comparison, e.g. response, remission or deterioration. This is variable is particularly relevant for dichotomous effect size data, because it indicates what the event counts refer to. The msd factor level is typically used for outcomes expressed in means and standard deviations.
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: This variable describes the instrument through which the relevant outcome was measured.
metadata/variable_description.json.time: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (e.g. post or follow-up).
metadata/variable_description.json.time_weeks: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained, in weeks after randomization (set to NA if this information was not available).
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: This variable encodes if the measured outcome was self-reported ("self-report") or clinician-rated ("clinician").
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_m_arm1: Mean of the outcome in the first arm at baseline.
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_m_arm2: Mean of the outcome in the second arm at baseline.
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_sd_arm1: Standard deviation of the outcome in the first arm at baseline.
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_sd_arm2: Standard deviation of the outcome in the second arm at baseline.
metadata/variable_description.json.mean_arm1: Mean of the outcome in the first arm at the measured time point.
metadata/variable_description.json.mean_arm2: Mean of the outcome in the second arm at the measured time point.
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_arm2: Standard deviation of the outcome in the second arm at the measured time point.
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_arm1: Standard deviation of the outcome in the first arm at the measured time point.
metadata/variable_description.json.n_arm1: Sample size in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.n_arm2: Sample size in the second trial arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.m_change_arm1: Mean score change between baseline and the measured time point in the first arm
metadata/variable_description.json.m_change_arm2: Mean score change between baseline and the measured time point in the second arm
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm1: Standard deviation of the mean change in the first arm
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm2: Standard deviation of the mean change in the second arm
metadata/variable_description.json.n_change_arm1: Sample size in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.n_change_arm2: Sample size in the second trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm1: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm2: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm1: Total sample size in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm2: Total sample size in the second trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_g: The pre-calculated value of Hedges' g (small-sample bias corrected standardized mean difference
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr: The pre-calculated value of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr_se: The standard error of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm
metadata/variable_description.json..id: Unique identifier for a trial arm comparison/row
metadata/variable_description.json..g: Calculated effect size (Hedges' g)
metadata/variable_description.json..g_se: Standard error of Hedges' g
metadata/variable_description.json..log_rr: Calculated effect size (logeRR)
metadata/variable_description.json..log_rr_se: Standard error of logeRR
metadata/variable_description.json.rob_domain1: risk of bias (version 2) rating domain 1: randomization process. This includes low risk of bias, high risk of bias, and some concerns.
metadata/variable_description.json.rob_domain2: risk of bias (version 2) rating domain 2: deviation from intended treatment. This includes low risk of bias, high risk of bias, and some concerns.
metadata/variable_description.json.rob_domain3: risk of bias (version 2) rating domain 3: dealing with missing outcome data. This includes low risk of bias, high risk of bias, and some concerns.
metadata/variable_description.json.rob_domain4: risk of bias (version 2) rating domain 4: measurement of the outcomes. This includes low risk of bias, high risk of bias, and some concerns.
metadata/variable_description.json.rob_domain5: risk of bias (version 2) rating domain 5: selection of the reported results. This includes low risk of bias, high risk of bias, and some concerns.
metadata/variable_description.json.rob_overall: The overall risk of bias (version 2) based on the five domains. This includes the low risk of bias, high risk of bias, and some concerns.

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-ptsd-mdmactr: Version 26.0.0
metadata.description:
The data-ptsd-mdmactr dataset 📊

The data-ptsd-mdmactr dataset is a meta-analytic research domain (MARD) on MDMA therapies for adults with post-traumatic stress disorder. This MARD is part of the Metapsy project. The date of the last search update is provided here. This dataset includes MDMA therapy vs. control ('mdma vs ctr') comparisons. Effect sizes are provided for outcomes at post-test and long-term follow-ups, if available.

This living database has been developed by the Sypres (Synthesis of Psychedelic Research Studies) Collaboration. Further information on Sypres and its underlying methodology can be found in this published article.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard. All included information has been independently extracted two researchers. Risk of bias ratings were conducted using the Cochrane Collaboration Risk of Bias Tool (Version 2).

metadata/variable_description.json.study: Author of the study and year of publication
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm1: condition in the first arm (mdma = MDMA)
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: condition in the second arm (pcb = placebo)
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: distinguishes arms in multi-arm studies (e.g. dose of MDMA)
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: distinguishes arms in multi-arm studies (e.g. dose of MDMA)
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: how the outcome is reported (change = change from baseline score, msd = endpoint mean and standard deviation, response = response (dichotomous outcome), remission = remission (dichotomous outcome)
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: instrument used to measure outcome
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: describes who administers or completes the instrument (clinician = clinician-rated scale, self-report = self-report scale)
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument_symptom: describes the symptom the instrument surveys (PTSD)
metadata/variable_description.json.primary_instrument: describes if the instrument listed was reported as or chosen as the primary outcome instrument (1 = yes, 0 = no)
metadata/variable_description.json.cov_time_point: timepoint at which the outcome measure was taken according to Covidence data extraction template timepoint
metadata/variable_description.json.study_time_point: timepoint at which the outcome measure was taken as reported in the paper and listed in Covidence
metadata/variable_description.json.time_weeks: timepoint at which the outcome measure was taken in weeks, relative to baseline
metadata/variable_description.json.time_days: timepoint at which the outcome measure was taken in days, relative to baseline
metadata/variable_description.json.primary_timepoint: describes if the timepoint listed was reported as or chosen as the primary timepoint (1 = yes, 0 = no)
metadata/variable_description.json.post_crossover: describes if the timepoint listed corresponds to a time before crossover or after crossover (0 = before crossover, 1 = after crossover, NA = does not correspond to a crossover study design
metadata/variable_description.json.n_arm1: number of participants in arm 1 (for endpoint studies)
metadata/variable_description.json.mean_arm1: mean value in arm 1 (for endpoint studies)
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_arm1: standard deviation of mean value in arm 1 (for endpoint studies)
metadata/variable_description.json.n_arm2: number of participants in arm 2 (for endpoint studies)
metadata/variable_description.json.mean_arm2: mean value in arm 2 (for endpoint studies)
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_arm2: standard deviation of mean value in arm 2 (for endpoint studies)
metadata/variable_description.json.n_change_arm1: number of participants in arm 1 (for change from baseline studies)
metadata/variable_description.json.mean_change_arm1: mean value in arm 1 (for change from baseline studies)
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm1: standard deviation of mean value in arm 1 (for change from baseline studies)
metadata/variable_description.json.n_change_arm2: number of participants in arm 2 (for change from baseline studies)
metadata/variable_description.json.mean_change_arm2: mean value in arm 2 (for change from baseline studies)
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm2: standard deviation of mean value in arm 2 (for change from baseline studies)
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm1: number of events in arm 1 (for dichotomous outcomes)
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm1: total number of participants in arm 1 (for dichotomous outcomes)
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm2: number of events in arm 2 (for dichotomous outcomes)
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm2: total number of participants in arm 2 (for dichotomous outcomes)
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_m_arm1: mean value at baseline timepoint for arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_sd_arm1: standard deviation of mean value at baseline timepoint for arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm1: number of participants in arm 1 at baseline timepoint
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_m_arm2: mean value at baseline timepoint for arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_sd_arm2: standard deviation of mean value at baseline timepoint for arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm2: number of participants in arm 2 at baseline timempoint
metadata/variable_description.json.d1: risk of bias rating for domain 1 (randomization process)
metadata/variable_description.json.d2: risk of bias rating for domain 2 (deviations from intended interventions)
metadata/variable_description.json.d3: risk of bias rating for domain 3 (missing outcome data)
metadata/variable_description.json.d4: risk of bias rating for domain 4 (outcome measurement)

metadata/variable_description.json..event_arm1: calculated number of events in arm 1 (see event_arm1)

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-dep-perinatal-psyctr: Version 26.0.1
metadata.description:
The data-dep-perinatal-psyctr dataset 📊

The data-perinatal-depression dataset is part of the meta-analytic research domain (MARD) on psychological interventions for perinatal depression. This MARD is part of the Metapsy project. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of perinatal depression psychological intervention trials. The date of the last search update is provided here.

This dataset includes lifestyle vs. control (ls vs ctr); music therapy vs. control (msc vs ctr); nutrition vs. control (nut vs ctr); physical activity vs. control (pa vs ctr); psychosocial vs. control (psc vs ctr); and psychotherapy vs. control (psy vs ctr) comparisons (this information is included in the comparison column).

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.
