metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm1: Type of treatment (cbt= cognitive behaviour therapy, bat= behavioural activation, pst= problem solving therapy, ipt= interpersonal psychotherapy, dyn= psychodynamic therapy, lrt= life review therapy, other psy= other type of psychotherapy)
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: Type of comparator (cau= care as usual, wl= waitlist,  pha= pharmacological treatment, other ctr= other type of inactive control grou, sup= supportive counseling, other psy= other type of psychotherapy )
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the first arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of CBT interventions, face-to-face and Internet-based, this variable would be set to f2f and Internet, respectively.
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the second arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of control groups, waitlist and placebo, this variable would be set to wl and plac, respectively. Typically, multiarm trials employ two or more active treatments (e.g. CBT and problem-solving therapy), which are compared to the same control group (e.g. a waitlist). This means that values in multi_arm2 do not differ (e.g. they are always wl for this specific multiarm trial); nevertheless, the variable should be specified in the dataset.
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: This variable encodes the type of outcome that builds the basis of the comparison, e.g. means and standard deviations (msd), change from baseline, response, remission, other statistics, etc.
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: This variable describes the instrument through which the relevant outcome was measured.
metadata/variable_description.json.time: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (e.g. post or follow-up).
metadata/variable_description.json.time_weeks: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained, in weeks after randomization (set to NA if this information was not available).
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: This variable encodes if the measured outcome was self-reported ("self-report") or clinician-rated ("clinician").
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm1: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm2: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm1: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm2: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm1: Total number of participants arm 1 (event data)
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm2: Total number of participants arm 2 (event data)
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_g: The pre-calculated value of Hedges' g (small-sample bias corrected standardized mean difference; Hedges, 1981).
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr: The pre-calculated value of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr_se: The standard error of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm1: Number of participants at baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm2: Number of participants at baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.dich: Exact definition of the dichotomous outcome as provided in the publication: e.g."remission based on bdi-II<=8 and ham-d<=7"
metadata/variable_description.json.dich_type: Broader categories of dichotomous outcomes: remission, response, etc.
metadata/variable_description.json.comorbid_mental: All the participants are recruited based on meeting criteria for a comorbid mental health disorder (e.g. anxiety and depression). Coded as y= yes, n= no
metadata/variable_description.json.format: ind= individual; grp= group; gsh= guided self-help; tel= telephone; cpl= couple therapy; oth= other (mixed formats); ush= unguided self-help
metadata/variable_description.json.format_details: It includes more details about the format, when necessary

metadata/variable_description.json.sg: Sequence generation (0= high risk; 1= low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.ba: Blinding of assessors (0= high risk; 1= low risk; sr= self-report)
metadata/variable_description.json.itt: Intention-to-treat analyses (0= high risk; 1= low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.rob: Overall risk of bias score. ranging from 0 (high risk) to 4 (low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.no.arms: Number of arms with the same measurement instrument within a study

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-depression-anxiety-transdiagnostic: Version 22.0.5
metadata.description:
The data-transdiagnostic-depression-anxiety dataset 📊

The data-transdiagnostic-depression-anxiety dataset is part of the meta-analytic research domain (MARD) on psychotherapy for depression/anxiety. This MARD is part of the Metapsy project. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of transdiagnostic psychological interventions for depression and anxiety. The date of the last search update is provided here.

This dataset includes psychotherapy vs. control (psy vs ctr) comparisons. Effect sizes are provided for depression and anxiety outcomes at post-test. It includes one type of effect size calculation per study, giving priority to means and standard deviations at post-test, followed by change scores, binary outcomes, and other statistics.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.

metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm1: Type of treatment (cbt= cognitive behaviour therapy, bat= behavioural activation, pst= problem solving therapy, ipt= interpersonal psychotherapy, dyn= psychodynamic therapy, lrt= life review therapy, other psy= other type of psychotherapy)
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: Type of comparator (cau= care as usual, wl= waitlist,  pha= pharmacological treatment, other ctr= other type of inactive control grou, sup= supportive counseling, other psy= other type of psychotherapy )
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the first arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of CBT interventions, face-to-face and Internet-based, this variable would be set to f2f and Internet, respectively.
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the second arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of control groups, waitlist and placebo, this variable would be set to wl and plac, respectively. Typically, multiarm trials employ two or more active treatments (e.g. CBT and problem-solving therapy), which are compared to the same control group (e.g. a waitlist). This means that values in multi_arm2 do not differ (e.g. they are always wl for this specific multiarm trial); nevertheless, the variable should be specified in the dataset.
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: This variable encodes the type of outcome that builds the basis of the comparison, e.g. means and standard deviations (msd), change from baseline, response, remission, other statistics, etc.
metadata/variable_description.json.sample: Indicates whether the extracted data is obtained from intention to treat estimates or from observed data.
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: This variable describes the instrument through which the relevant outcome was measured.
metadata/variable_description.json.time: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (e.g. post or follow-up).
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: This variable encodes if the measured outcome was self-reported ("self-report") or clinician-rated ("clinician").
metadata/variable_description.json.depanx: Indicates whether the effect size is calculated based on anxiety, depression, or mixed anxiety and depression measures
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm1: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm2: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm1: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm2: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm1: Total number of participants arm 1 (event data). Randomized sample.
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm2: Total number of participants arm 2 (event data). Randomized sample.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_g: The pre-calculated value of Hedges' g (small-sample bias corrected standardized mean difference; Hedges, 1981).
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr: The pre-calculated value of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr_se: The standard error of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm1: Number of participants at baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm2: Number of participants at baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.dich: Exact definition of the dichotomous outcome as provided in the publication: e.g."remission based on bdi-II<=8 and ham-d<=7"
metadata/variable_description.json.dich_type: Broader categories of dichotomous outcomes: remission, response, etc.
metadata/variable_description.json.time_weeks: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained, in weeks after randomization (set to NA if this information was not available).
metadata/variable_description.json.comorbid_mental: All the participants are recruited based on meeting criteria for a comorbid mental health disorder (e.g. anxiety and depression). Coded as y= yes, n= no
metadata/variable_description.json.format: ind= individual; grp= group; gsh= guided self-help; tel= telephone; cpl= couple therapy; oth= other (mixed formats); ush= unguided self-help
metadata/variable_description.json.format_details: It includes more details about the format, when necessary
metadata/variable_description.json.country: us= USA; uk= United Kingdom; eu= Europe; can= Canada; au= australia; eas= east asia; oth= other
metadata/variable_description.json.age_group: adul= adults, 5= older adults (≥55 years); old= older old adults (≥75 years)
metadata/variable_description.json.recruitment: com= community; clin= clinical; oth= other
metadata/variable_description.json.diagnosis: mdd= major depression; mood= mood disorder; cut= cut-off score; sub= subclinical depression;chr= chronic depression
metadata/variable_description.json.target_group: adul= adults, old= older adults, stud= student population, ppd= women with perinatal depression; med= comorbid medical disorder; oth= other
metadata/variable_description.json.ac: Allocation concealment (0= high risk; 1= low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.sg: Sequence generation (0= high risk; 1= low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.ba: Blinding of assessors (0= high risk; 1= low risk; sr= self-report)
metadata/variable_description.json.itt: Intention-to-treat analyses (0= high risk; 1= low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.rob: Overall risk of bias score. ranging from 0 (high risk) to 4 (low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.no.arms: Number of arms with the same measurement instrument within a study
metadata/variable_description.json.primary: One primary outcome per study, based on a predefined hierarchy: HAM-D, BDI (I or II), another clinician-rated instrument, another self-report instrument, with priority for: PHQ-9, CES-D, HADS, GDS, EPDS, MMPI
metadata/variable_description.json.primary_calc: One primary calculation type per study based on the following hierarchy: 1) continuous, 2) dichotomous, 3) change from baseline, 4) other reported statistics

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-depression-anxiety-transdiagnostic: Version 22.0.4
metadata.description:
The data-transdiagnostic-depression-anxiety dataset 📊

The data-transdiagnostic-depression-anxiety dataset is part of the meta-analytic research domain (MARD) on psychotherapy for depression/anxiety. This MARD is part of the Metapsy project. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of transdiagnostic psychological interventions for depression and anxiety. The date of the last search update is provided here.

This dataset includes psychotherapy vs. control (psy vs ctr) comparisons. Effect sizes are provided for depression and anxiety outcomes at post-test. It includes one type of effect size calculation per study, giving priority to means and standard deviations at post-test, followed by change scores, binary outcomes, and other statistics.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.

metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm1: Type of treatment (cbt= cognitive behaviour therapy, bat= behavioural activation, pst= problem solving therapy, ipt= interpersonal psychotherapy, dyn= psychodynamic therapy, lrt= life review therapy, other psy= other type of psychotherapy)
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: Type of comparator (cau= care as usual, wl= waitlist,  pha= pharmacological treatment, other ctr= other type of inactive control grou, sup= supportive counseling, other psy= other type of psychotherapy )
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the first arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of CBT interventions, face-to-face and Internet-based, this variable would be set to f2f and Internet, respectively.
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the second arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of control groups, waitlist and placebo, this variable would be set to wl and plac, respectively. Typically, multiarm trials employ two or more active treatments (e.g. CBT and problem-solving therapy), which are compared to the same control group (e.g. a waitlist). This means that values in multi_arm2 do not differ (e.g. they are always wl for this specific multiarm trial); nevertheless, the variable should be specified in the dataset.
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: This variable encodes the type of outcome that builds the basis of the comparison, e.g. means and standard deviations (msd), change from baseline, response, remission, other statistics, etc.
metadata/variable_description.json.sample: Indicates whether the extracted data is obtained from intention to treat estimates or from observed data.
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: This variable describes the instrument through which the relevant outcome was measured.
metadata/variable_description.json.time: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (e.g. post or follow-up).
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: This variable encodes if the measured outcome was self-reported ("self-report") or clinician-rated ("clinician").
metadata/variable_description.json.depanx: Indicates whether the effect size is calculated based on anxiety, depression, or mixed anxiety and depression measures
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm1: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm2: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm1: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm2: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm1: Total number of participants arm 1 (event data). Randomized sample.
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm2: Total number of participants arm 2 (event data). Randomized sample.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_g: The pre-calculated value of Hedges' g (small-sample bias corrected standardized mean difference; Hedges, 1981).
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr: The pre-calculated value of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr_se: The standard error of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm1: Number of participants at baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm2: Number of participants at baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.dich: Exact definition of the dichotomous outcome as provided in the publication: e.g."remission based on bdi-II<=8 and ham-d<=7"

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-depression-anxiety-transdiagnostic: Version 22.0.3
metadata.description:
The data-transdiagnostic-depression-anxiety dataset 📊

The data-transdiagnostic-depression-anxiety dataset is part of the meta-analytic research domain (MARD) on psychotherapy for depression/anxiety. This MARD is part of the Metapsy project. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of transdiagnostic psychological interventions for depression and anxiety. The date of the last search update is provided here.

This dataset includes psychotherapy vs. control (psy vs ctr) comparisons. Effect sizes are provided for depression and anxiety outcomes at post-test. It includes one type of effect size calculation per study, giving priority to means and standard deviations at post-test, followed by change scores, binary outcomes, and other statistics.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.

metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm1: Type of treatment (cbt= cognitive behaviour therapy, bat= behavioural activation, pst= problem solving therapy, ipt= interpersonal psychotherapy, dyn= psychodynamic therapy, lrt= life review therapy, other psy= other type of psychotherapy)
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: Type of comparator (cau= care as usual, wl= waitlist,  pha= pharmacological treatment, other ctr= other type of inactive control grou, sup= supportive counseling, other psy= other type of psychotherapy )
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the first arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of CBT interventions, face-to-face and Internet-based, this variable would be set to f2f and Internet, respectively.
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the second arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of control groups, waitlist and placebo, this variable would be set to wl and plac, respectively. Typically, multiarm trials employ two or more active treatments (e.g. CBT and problem-solving therapy), which are compared to the same control group (e.g. a waitlist). This means that values in multi_arm2 do not differ (e.g. they are always wl for this specific multiarm trial); nevertheless, the variable should be specified in the dataset.
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: This variable encodes the type of outcome that builds the basis of the comparison, e.g. means and standard deviations (msd), change from baseline, response, remission, other statistics, etc.
metadata/variable_description.json.sample: Indicates whether the extracted data is obtained from intention to treat estimates or from observed data.
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: This variable describes the instrument through which the relevant outcome was measured.
metadata/variable_description.json.time: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (e.g. post or follow-up).
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: This variable encodes if the measured outcome was self-reported ("self-report") or clinician-rated ("clinician").
metadata/variable_description.json.depanx: Indicates whether the effect size is calculated based on anxiety, depression, or mixed anxiety and depression measures
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm1: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm2: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm1: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm2: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm1: Total number of participants arm 1 (event data). Randomized sample.
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm2: Total number of participants arm 2 (event data). Randomized sample.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_g: The pre-calculated value of Hedges' g (small-sample bias corrected standardized mean difference; Hedges, 1981).
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr: The pre-calculated value of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr_se: The standard error of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm1: Number of participants at baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm2: Number of participants at baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.dich: Exact definition of the dichotomous outcome as provided in the publication: e.g."remission based on bdi-II<=8 and ham-d<=7"
metadata/variable_description.json.dich_type: Broader categories of dichotomous outcomes: remission, response, etc.
metadata/variable_description.json.time_weeks: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained, in weeks after randomization (set to NA if this information was not available).
metadata/variable_description.json.comorbid_mental: All the participants are recruited based on meeting criteria for a comorbid mental health disorder (e.g. anxiety and depression). Coded as y= yes, n= no
metadata/variable_description.json.format: ind= individual; grp= group; gsh= guided self-help; tel= telephone; cpl= couple therapy; oth= other (mixed formats); ush= unguided self-help
metadata/variable_description.json.format_details: It includes more details about the format, when necessary
metadata/variable_description.json.country: us= USA; uk= United Kingdom; eu= Europe; can= Canada; au= australia; eas= east asia; oth= other
metadata/variable_description.json.age_group: adul= adults, 5= older adults (≥55 years); old= older old adults (≥75 years)
metadata/variable_description.json.recruitment: com= community; clin= clinical; oth= other
metadata/variable_description.json.diagnosis: mdd= major depression; mood= mood disorder; cut= cut-off score; sub= subclinical depression;chr= chronic depression
metadata/variable_description.json.target_group: adul= adults, old= older adults, stud= student population, ppd= women with perinatal depression; med= comorbid medical disorder; oth= other
metadata/variable_description.json.ac: Allocation concealment (0= high risk; 1= low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.sg: Sequence generation (0= high risk; 1= low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.ba: Blinding of assessors (0= high risk; 1= low risk; sr= self-report)
metadata/variable_description.json.itt: Intention-to-treat analyses (0= high risk; 1= low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.rob: Overall risk of bias score. ranging from 0 (high risk) to 4 (low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.no.arms: Number of arms with the same measurement instrument within a study
metadata/variable_description.json.primary: One primary outcome per study, based on a predefined hierarchy: HAM-D, BDI (I or II), another clinician-rated instrument, another self-report instrument, with priority for: PHQ-9, CES-D, HADS, GDS, EPDS, MMPI
metadata/variable_description.json.primary_calc: One primary calculation type per study based on the following hierarchy: 1) continuous, 2) dichotomous, 3) change from baseline, 4) other reported statistics

metadata/variable_description.json..g_se: metapsyTools generated variable: Standard error of Hedges' g.
metadata/variable_description.json..log_rr: metapsyTools generated variable: Calculated effect size (logeRR).
metadata/variable_description.json..log_rr_se: metapsyTools generated variable: Standard error of logeRR.

metadata/variable_description.json..event_arm2: metapsyTools generated variable: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm.

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-depression-anxiety-transdiagnostic: Version 22.0.2
metadata.description:
The data-transdiagnostic-depression-anxiety dataset 📊

The data-transdiagnostic-depression-anxiety dataset is part of the meta-analytic research domain (MARD) on psychotherapy for depression/anxiety. This MARD is part of the Metapsy project. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of transdiagnostic psychological interventions for depression and anxiety. The date of the last search update is provided here.

This dataset includes psychotherapy vs. control (psy vs ctr) comparisons. Effect sizes are provided for depression and anxiety outcomes at post-test. It includes one type of effect size calculation per study, giving priority to means and standard deviations at post-test, followed by change scores, binary outcomes, and other statistics.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.

metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm1: Type of treatment (cbt= cognitive behaviour therapy, bat= behavioural activation, pst= problem solving therapy, ipt= interpersonal psychotherapy, dyn= psychodynamic therapy, lrt= life review therapy, other psy= other type of psychotherapy)
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: Type of comparator (cau= care as usual, wl= waitlist,  pha= pharmacological treatment, other ctr= other type of inactive control grou, sup= supportive counseling, other psy= other type of psychotherapy )
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the first arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of CBT interventions, face-to-face and Internet-based, this variable would be set to f2f and Internet, respectively.
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the second arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of control groups, waitlist and placebo, this variable would be set to wl and plac, respectively. Typically, multiarm trials employ two or more active treatments (e.g. CBT and problem-solving therapy), which are compared to the same control group (e.g. a waitlist). This means that values in multi_arm2 do not differ (e.g. they are always wl for this specific multiarm trial); nevertheless, the variable should be specified in the dataset.
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: This variable encodes the type of outcome that builds the basis of the comparison, e.g. means and standard deviations (msd), change from baseline, response, remission, other statistics, etc.
metadata/variable_description.json.sample: Indicates whether the extracted data is obtained from intention to treat estimates or from observed data.
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: This variable describes the instrument through which the relevant outcome was measured.
metadata/variable_description.json.time: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (e.g. post or follow-up).
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: This variable encodes if the measured outcome was self-reported ("self-report") or clinician-rated ("clinician").
metadata/variable_description.json.depanx: Indicates whether the effect size is calculated based on anxiety, depression, or mixed anxiety and depression measures
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm1: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm2: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm1: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm2: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm1: Total number of participants arm 1 (event data). Randomized sample.
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm2: Total number of participants arm 2 (event data). Randomized sample.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_g: The pre-calculated value of Hedges' g (small-sample bias corrected standardized mean difference; Hedges, 1981).
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr: The pre-calculated value of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr_se: The standard error of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm1: Number of participants at baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm2: Number of participants at baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.dich: Exact definition of the dichotomous outcome as provided in the publication: e.g."remission based on bdi-II<=8 and ham-d<=7"
metadata/variable_description.json.dich_type: Broader categories of dichotomous outcomes: remission, response, etc.
metadata/variable_description.json.time_weeks: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained, in weeks after randomization (set to NA if this information was not available).
metadata/variable_description.json.comorbid_mental: All the participants are recruited based on meeting criteria for a comorbid mental health disorder (e.g. anxiety and depression). Coded as y= yes, n= no

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-depression-anxiety-transdiagnostic: Version 22.0.1
metadata.description:
The data-transdiagnostic-depression-anxiety dataset 📊

The data-transdiagnostic-depression-anxiety dataset is part of the meta-analytic research domain (MARD) on psychotherapy for depression/anxiety. This MARD is part of the Metapsy project. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of transdiagnostic psychological interventions for depression and anxiety. The date of the last search update is provided here.

This dataset includes psychotherapy vs. control (psy vs ctr) comparisons. Effect sizes are provided for depression and anxiety outcomes at post-test. It includes one type of effect size calculation per study, giving priority to means and standard deviations at post-test, followed by change scores, binary outcomes, and other statistics.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.

metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm1: Type of treatment (cbt= cognitive behaviour therapy, bat= behavioural activation, pst= problem solving therapy, ipt= interpersonal psychotherapy, dyn= psychodynamic therapy, lrt= life review therapy, other psy= other type of psychotherapy)
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: Type of comparator (cau= care as usual, wl= waitlist,  pha= pharmacological treatment, other ctr= other type of inactive control grou, sup= supportive counseling, other psy= other type of psychotherapy )
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the first arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of CBT interventions, face-to-face and Internet-based, this variable would be set to f2f and Internet, respectively.
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the second arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of control groups, waitlist and placebo, this variable would be set to wl and plac, respectively. Typically, multiarm trials employ two or more active treatments (e.g. CBT and problem-solving therapy), which are compared to the same control group (e.g. a waitlist). This means that values in multi_arm2 do not differ (e.g. they are always wl for this specific multiarm trial); nevertheless, the variable should be specified in the dataset.
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: This variable encodes the type of outcome that builds the basis of the comparison, e.g. means and standard deviations (msd), change from baseline, response, remission, other statistics, etc.
metadata/variable_description.json.sample: Indicates whether the extracted data is obtained from intention to treat estimates or from observed data.
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: This variable describes the instrument through which the relevant outcome was measured.
metadata/variable_description.json.time: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (e.g. post or follow-up).
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: This variable encodes if the measured outcome was self-reported ("self-report") or clinician-rated ("clinician").
metadata/variable_description.json.depanx: Indicates whether the effect size is calculated based on anxiety, depression, or mixed anxiety and depression measures
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm1: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm2: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm1: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm2: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm1: Total number of participants arm 1 (event data). Randomized sample.
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm2: Total number of participants arm 2 (event data). Randomized sample.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_g: The pre-calculated value of Hedges' g (small-sample bias corrected standardized mean difference; Hedges, 1981).
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr: The pre-calculated value of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr_se: The standard error of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm1: Number of participants at baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm2: Number of participants at baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.dich: Exact definition of the dichotomous outcome as provided in the publication: e.g."remission based on bdi-II<=8 and ham-d<=7"
metadata/variable_description.json.dich_type: Broader categories of dichotomous outcomes: remission, response, etc.
metadata/variable_description.json.time_weeks: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained, in weeks after randomization (set to NA if this information was not available).
metadata/variable_description.json.comorbid_mental: All the participants are recruited based on meeting criteria for a comorbid mental health disorder (e.g. anxiety and depression). Coded as y= yes, n= no
metadata/variable_description.json.format: ind= individual; grp= group; gsh= guided self-help; tel= telephone; cpl= couple therapy; oth= other (mixed formats); ush= unguided self-help
metadata/variable_description.json.format_details: It includes more details about the format, when necessary
metadata/variable_description.json.country: us= USA; uk= United Kingdom; eu= Europe; can= Canada; au= australia; eas= east asia; oth= other
metadata/variable_description.json.age_group: adul= adults, 5= older adults (≥55 years); old= older old adults (≥75 years)
metadata/variable_description.json.recruitment: com= community; clin= clinical; oth= other
metadata/variable_description.json.diagnosis: mdd= major depression; mood= mood disorder; cut= cut-off score; sub= subclinical depression;chr= chronic depression
metadata/variable_description.json.target_group: adul= adults, old= older adults, stud= student population, ppd= women with perinatal depression; med= comorbid medical disorder; oth= other
metadata/variable_description.json.ac: Allocation concealment (0= high risk; 1= low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.sg: Sequence generation (0= high risk; 1= low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.ba: Blinding of assessors (0= high risk; 1= low risk; sr= self-report)
metadata/variable_description.json.itt: Intention-to-treat analyses (0= high risk; 1= low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.rob: Overall risk of bias score. ranging from 0 (high risk) to 4 (low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.no.arms: Number of arms with the same measurement instrument within a study
metadata/variable_description.json.primary: One primary outcome per study, based on a predefined hierarchy: HAM-D, BDI (I or II), another clinician-rated instrument, another self-report instrument, with priority for: PHQ-9, CES-D, HADS, GDS, EPDS, MMPI
metadata/variable_description.json.primary_calc: One primary calculation type per study based on the following hierarchy: 1) continuous, 2) dichotomous, 3) change from baseline, 4) other reported statistics

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-depression-inpatients: Version 22.2.1
metadata.description:
The data-depression-inpatients dataset 📊

The data-depression-inpatients dataset is part of the meta-analytic research domain (MARD) on psychotherapy for depression. This MARD is part of the Metapsy project. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of depression psychotherapy trials in inpatients. The date of the last search update is provided here.

This dataset includes psychotherapy vs. control (psy vs ctr) and psychotherapy vs. psychotherapy comparisons (psy vs psy; this information is included in the comparison column). It also includes multiple outcome calculation types within studies (e.g. means and SD and remission), which can be filtered with the "primary_outcome_type" variable.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.

metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm1: Type of treatment (cbt= cognitive behaviour therapy, bat= behavioural activation, pst= problem solving therapy, ipt= interpersonal psychotherapy, dyn= psychodynamic therapy, lrt= life review therapy, other psy= other type of psychotherapy)
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: Type of comparator (cau= care as usual, wl= waitlist,  pha= pharmacological treatment, other ctr= other type of inactive control grou, sup= supportive counseling, other psy= other type of psychotherapy )
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the first arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of CBT interventions, face-to-face and Internet-based, this variable would be set to f2f and Internet, respectively.
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the second arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of control groups, waitlist and placebo, this variable would be set to wl and plac, respectively. Typically, multiarm trials employ two or more active treatments (e.g. CBT and problem-solving therapy), which are compared to the same control group (e.g. a waitlist). This means that values in multi_arm2 do not differ (e.g. they are always wl for this specific multiarm trial); nevertheless, the variable should be specified in the dataset.
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: This variable encodes the type of outcome that builds the basis of the comparison, e.g. response, remission or deterioration. This is variable is particularly relevant for dichotomous effect size data, because it indicates what the event counts refer to. The msd factor level is typically used for outcomes expressed in means and standard deviations.
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: This variable describes the instrument through which the relevant outcome was measured.
metadata/variable_description.json.time: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (e.g. post or follow-up).
metadata/variable_description.json.time_weeks: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained, in weeks after randomization (set to NA if this information was not available).
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: This variable encodes if the measured outcome was self-reported ("self-report") or clinician-rated ("clinician").
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm1: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm2: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm1: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm2: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm1: Total number of participants arm 1 (event data)
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm2: Total number of participants arm 2 (event data)
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_g: The pre-calculated value of Hedges' g (small-sample bias corrected standardized mean difference; Hedges, 1981).
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr: The pre-calculated value of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr_se: The standard error of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm1: Number of participants at baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm2: Number of participants at baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.dich: Exact definition of the dichotomous outcome as provided in the publication: e.g."remission based on bdi-II<=8 and ham-d<=7"
metadata/variable_description.json.dich_type: Broader categories of dichotomous outcomes: remission, response, etc.
metadata/variable_description.json.comorbid_mental: All the participants are recruited based on meeting criteria for a comorbid mental health disorder (e.g. anxiety and depression). Coded as y= yes, n= no

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-inpatients: Version 22.2.0
metadata.description:
The data-inpatients dataset 📊

<img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/DOI-10.5281%2Fzenodo.6881064-blue">

The data-inpatients dataset is part of the meta-analytic research domain (MARD) on psychotherapy for depression. This MARD is part of the Metapsy project. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of depression psychotherapy trials in inpatients. The date of the last search update is provided here.

This dataset includes psychotherapy vs. control (psy vs ctr) and psychotherapy vs. psychotherapy comparisons (psy vs psy; this information is included in the comparison column). It also includes multiple outcome calculation types within studies (e.g. means and SD and remission), which can be filtered with the "primary_outcome_type" variable.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.

metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm1: Type of treatment (cbt= cognitive behaviour therapy, bat= behavioural activation, pst= problem solving therapy, ipt= interpersonal psychotherapy, dyn= psychodynamic therapy, lrt= life review therapy, other psy= other type of psychotherapy)
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: Type of comparator (cau= care as usual, wl= waitlist,  pha= pharmacological treatment, other ctr= other type of inactive control grou, sup= supportive counseling, other psy= other type of psychotherapy )
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the first arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of CBT interventions, face-to-face and Internet-based, this variable would be set to f2f and Internet, respectively.
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the second arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of control groups, waitlist and placebo, this variable would be set to wl and plac, respectively. Typically, multiarm trials employ two or more active treatments (e.g. CBT and problem-solving therapy), which are compared to the same control group (e.g. a waitlist). This means that values in multi_arm2 do not differ (e.g. they are always wl for this specific multiarm trial); nevertheless, the variable should be specified in the dataset.
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: This variable encodes the type of outcome that builds the basis of the comparison, e.g. response, remission or deterioration. This is variable is particularly relevant for dichotomous effect size data, because it indicates what the event counts refer to. The msd factor level is typically used for outcomes expressed in means and standard deviations.
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: This variable describes the instrument through which the relevant outcome was measured.
metadata/variable_description.json.time: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (e.g. post or follow-up).
metadata/variable_description.json.time_weeks: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained, in weeks after randomization (set to NA if this information was not available).
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: This variable encodes if the measured outcome was self-reported ("self-report") or clinician-rated ("clinician").
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm1: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm2: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm1: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm2: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm1: Total number of participants arm 1 (event data)
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm2: Total number of participants arm 2 (event data)
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_g: The pre-calculated value of Hedges' g (small-sample bias corrected standardized mean difference; Hedges, 1981).
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr: The pre-calculated value of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr_se: The standard error of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm1: Number of participants at baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm2: Number of participants at baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.dich: Exact definition of the dichotomous outcome as provided in the publication: e.g."remission based on bdi-II<=8 and ham-d<=7"
metadata/variable_description.json.dich_type: Broader categories of dichotomous outcomes: remission, response, etc.
metadata/variable_description.json.comorbid_mental: All the participants are recruited based on meeting criteria for a comorbid mental health disorder (e.g. anxiety and depression). Coded as y= yes, n= no
metadata/variable_description.json.format: ind= individual; grp= group; gsh= guided self-help; tel= telephone; cpl= couple therapy; oth= other (mixed formats); ush= unguided self-help
metadata/variable_description.json.format_details: It includes more details about the format, when necessary
metadata/variable_description.json.country: us= USA; uk= United Kingdom; eu= Europe; can= Canada; au= australia; eas= east asia; oth= other
metadata/variable_description.json.age_group: adul= adults, 5= older adults (≥55 years); old= older old adults (≥75 years)
metadata/variable_description.json.recruitment: com= community; clin= clinical; oth= other
metadata/variable_description.json.diagnosis: mdd= major depression; mood= mood disorder; cut= cut-off score; sub= subclinical depression;chr= chronic depression
metadata/variable_description.json.target_group: adul= adults, old= older adults, stud= student population, ppd= women with perinatal depression; med= comorbid medical disorder; oth= other
metadata/variable_description.json.ac: Allocation concealment (0= high risk; 1= low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.sg: Sequence generation (0= high risk; 1= low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.ba: Blinding of assessors (0= high risk; 1= low risk; sr= self-report)
metadata/variable_description.json.itt: Intention-to-treat analyses (0= high risk; 1= low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.rob: Overall risk of bias score. ranging from 0 (high risk) to 5 (low risk)
metadata/variable_description.json.no.arms: Number of arms with the same measurement instrument within a study
metadata/variable_description.json.primary: One primary outcome per study, based on a predefined hierarchy: HAM-D, BDI (I or II), another clinician-rated instrument, another self-report instrument, with priority for: PHQ-9, CES-D, HADS, GDS, EPDS, MMPI
metadata/variable_description.json.primary_calc: One primary calculation type per study based on the following hierarchy: 1) continuous, 2) dichotomous, 3) change from baseline, 4) other reported statistics
metadata/variable_description.json.comparison: Type of comparison: psychotherapy vs control, psychotherapy vs psychotherapy

metadata/variable_description.json..log_rr_se: metapsyTools generated variable: Standard error of logeRR.

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-inpatients: Version 22.1.0
metadata.description:
The data-inpatients dataset 📊

The data-inpatients dataset is part of the meta-analytic research domain (MARD) on psychotherapy for depression. This MARD is part of the Metapsy project. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of depression psychotherapy trials in inpatients. The date of the last search update is provided here.

This dataset includes psychotherapy vs. control (psy vs ctr) and psychotherapy vs. psychotherapy comparisons (psy vs psy; this information is included in the comparison column). It also includes multiple outcome calculation types within studies (e.g. means and SD and remission), which can be filtered with the "primary_outcome_type" variable.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.

metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm1: Type of treatment (cbt= cognitive behaviour therapy, bat= behavioural activation, pst= problem solving therapy, ipt= interpersonal psychotherapy, dyn= psychodynamic therapy, lrt= life review therapy, other psy= other type of psychotherapy)
metadata/variable_description.json.condition_arm2: Type of comparator (cau= care as usual, wl= waitlist,  pha= pharmacological treatment, other ctr= other type of inactive control grou, sup= supportive counseling, other psy= other type of psychotherapy )
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm1: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the first arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of CBT interventions, face-to-face and Internet-based, this variable would be set to f2f and Internet, respectively.
metadata/variable_description.json.multi_arm2: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the second arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of control groups, waitlist and placebo, this variable would be set to wl and plac, respectively. Typically, multiarm trials employ two or more active treatments (e.g. CBT and problem-solving therapy), which are compared to the same control group (e.g. a waitlist). This means that values in multi_arm2 do not differ (e.g. they are always wl for this specific multiarm trial); nevertheless, the variable should be specified in the dataset.
metadata/variable_description.json.outcome_type: This variable encodes the type of outcome that builds the basis of the comparison, e.g. response, remission or deterioration. This is variable is particularly relevant for dichotomous effect size data, because it indicates what the event counts refer to. The msd factor level is typically used for outcomes expressed in means and standard deviations.
metadata/variable_description.json.instrument: This variable describes the instrument through which the relevant outcome was measured.
metadata/variable_description.json.time: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (e.g. post or follow-up).
metadata/variable_description.json.time_weeks: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained, in weeks after randomization (set to NA if this information was not available).
metadata/variable_description.json.rating: This variable encodes if the measured outcome was self-reported ("self-report") or clinician-rated ("clinician").
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm1: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.sd_change_arm2: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm1: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.event_arm2: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm1: Total number of participants arm 1 (event data)
metadata/variable_description.json.totaln_arm2: Total number of participants arm 2 (event data)
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_g: The pre-calculated value of Hedges' g (small-sample bias corrected standardized mean difference; Hedges, 1981).
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr: The pre-calculated value of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.precalc_log_rr_se: The standard error of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm1: Number of participants at baseline arm 1
metadata/variable_description.json.baseline_n_arm2: Number of participants at baseline arm 2
metadata/variable_description.json.dich: Exact definition of the dichotomous outcome as provided in the publication: e.g."remission based on bdi-II<=8 and ham-d<=7"

metadata.title: metapsy-project/data-inpatients: Version 22.0.1
metadata.description:
The data-inpatients dataset 📊

The data-inpatients dataset is part of the meta-analytic research domain (MARD) on psychotherapy for depression. This MARD is part of the Metapsy project. The dataset contains study information and effect size data of depression psychotherapy trials in inpatients. The date of the last search update is provided here.

This dataset includes psychotherapy vs. control (psy vs ctr) and psychotherapy vs. psychotherapy comparisons (psy vs psy; this information is included in the comparison column). It also includes multiple outcome calculation types within studies (e.g. means and SD and remission), which can be filtered with the "primary_outcome_type" variable.

The dataset follows the Metapsy data standard.

metadata.title: metapsy-project/metapsyData: Version 0.2.1-1
metadata.description:
This package allows you to access the meta-analytic psychotherapy databases in R. To install the metapsyData package, use the following code:

if (!require("devtools"))
  install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("metapsy-project/metapsyData")

The metapsyData package allows to access the Metapsy meta-analytic psychotherapy databases direct in your R environment. Once installed, simply use the getData function and insert the database shorthand to save the data locally. The documentation of the package is also hosted by rdrr.io.

To search for available databases in metapsyData and their shorthands, run the listData() function. All databases included in metapsyData come with an extensive documentation entry on docs.metapsy.org.

Usage Example 
# List all available databases
listData()

# Get latest version of the 'depression-psyctr' database
d <- getData("depression-psyctr")

# Get version 22.2 of the 'depression-psyctr' database
d <- getData("depression-psyctr", version = "22.2")

# Show variable description
variableDescription(d)

# Open online documentation
openDocs(d)
Repository Rules

You are allowed to use, fork and share the package. Please note that we will not consider pull requests or issue reports from external users who are not part of the Metapsy project collaboration.

metadata.title: metapsy-project/metapsyData: Version 0.1.2
metadata.description:
The metapsyData package allows you to access the meta-analytic psychotherapy databases in R. The package lives in a GitHub repository. You can download this release using the code below:

if (!require("devtools"))
  install.packages("devtools")

devtools::install_github(
    "metapsy-project/metapsyData/tree/0.1.2")

The preferred citation for this version of the package is:

Harrer, M., Karyotaki, E., Cuijpers, P. (2022). metapsyData: Access the Meta-Analytic Psychotherapy Databases (Version 0.1.2). URL metapsy.org/r-package.

metadata.description:
The metapsyTools package facilitates the calculation of effect sizes and meta-analyses based on the Metapsy database (or databases adhering to the same format). The package lives in a GitHub repository. You can download this release using the code below:

    build_vignettes = TRUE)

The preferred citation for this version of the package is:

metadata.title: metapsy-project/metapsyTools: Version 0.3.3-3
metadata.description:
<h1> <code style="background: white;">metapsyTools</code> </h1> <a href='https://dplyr.tidyverse.org'><img src='https://tools.metapsy.org/logo.png' align="right" height="139" /></a>

The metapsyTools package facilitates the calculation of effect sizes and meta-analyses based on the Metapsy database (or databases adhering to the same format).

Installation

The metapsyTools package lives in a GitHub repository. It can only be downloaded using the code below:

if (!require("devtools"))
  install.packages("devtools")

devtools::install_github(
    "metapsy-project/metapsyTools",
    build_vignettes = TRUE)
Repository Rules

You are allowed to use, fork and share the package. Please note that we will not consider pull requests or issue reports from external users who are not part of the Metapsy project collaboration.

metadata.title: metapsyData: R Package to Access the Metapsy Databases
metadata.description:
The metapsyData package allows to access the Metapsy meta-analytic psychotherapy databases direct in your R environment. Once installed, simply run the data function (e.g. data(DepPsychDB)) to save the data locally. The documentation of the package is also hosted by rdrr.io.

The interactive Metapsy web application (metapsy.org) uses metapsyData in the background. You can open the Metapsy website in R by running open_app().

The raw data files can be accessed in the associated GitHub repository under data. To search for available databases in metapsyData, type in metapsyData:: in your RStudio console.
references: Harrer, M., Ebert, D. D., Karyotaki, E., Cuijpers, P. (2020). MetaPsyR: Access   the Meta-Analytic Psychotherapy Database. R package version 0.1.0. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.5171880.
